key_concepts: Atoms gain or lose valence electrons to achieve noble gas stability
Metals tend to lose electrons and form positive cations
Nonmetals tend to gain electrons and form negative anions
Group number indicates the number of valence electrons for representative elements
Electron dot structures represent valence electrons
Ionic bonding involves electron transfer from a metal to a nonmetal
Ionic compounds are electrically neutral combinations of cations and anions
Formula units show the lowest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound
Ionic compounds are named with the cation first and the anion ending in -ide
Charge balancing is used to predict formulas such as MgO, KCl, K3N, and Mg3N2
